newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Pepkor goes into banking.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Pepkor goes into banking.

text.p: Pepkor Ltd chairman Christo Wiese has added a new dimension to South African banking by negotiating a deal between NBS Holdings and Boland Bank Ltd that would provide in-store banking facilities in Pepkor retail outlets.
In the process, he has created South Africa's fifth largest bank with assets of about 26.5 billion rand.

Wiese, who is also chairman of Boland Bank, announced on Sunday that NBS Holdings (NBSH) would take over the entire banking and financial services interests of Boland Bank Holdings (BBH) in exchange for new NBSH shares.
This comes just over a week after Wiese announced that Boland Bank had acquired the right to buy 25.6 percent of NBS from Rand Merchant Bank Holdings.
This resulted in the issuing of new NBSH shares to BBH, which is 66.5 percent owned by Samgro Investment Holdings, also chaired by Wiese.

"The development is seen as one with far-reaching consequences for the country's financial services sector...(and) could prove to be but the first step in the establishment of a series of alliances of this nature," a joint BBH-NBSH statement said.

NBSH chairman Cedric Savage said the deal would benefit both businesses with "benefits such as an enhanced national branch network, efficient utilisation of common information technology platforms, the sharing of product technology and expertise and th pooling of management resources."

NBS would also gain access to Boland Bank's clearing, foreign exchange and card facilities. Boland Bank would benefit from NBS's expertise in mortgage lending, management information and cost control systems.

Boland Bank and NBS would continue to operate under their own names for the immediate future, but a task team had been set up to examine how best to maximise the benefits of the deal, the statement said.
The deal between NBSH and BBH still has to be ratified by shareholders, the Registrar of Banks and the Johannesburg Stock Exchange and is expected to go into effect on April 1.
